items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: heard Mary Lou Williams, a black piano player, wonderful, Edmund Thigpen on drums and Whitey Mitchell was on bass

ctx.x: Yeah, Charlie Parker, or well I remember taking my girlfriend, who later became my wife, her first experience in a jazz idiom in New York City we went to this place called The Composer and heard Mary Lou Williams, a black piano player, wonderful, Edmund Thigpen on drums and Whitey Mitchell was on bass. And she just really enjoyed that. But it was not Dixieland.
Right. Mary Lou Williams was fairly progressive always.
